title: Rigveda 9.17: To Soma
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 9.17: To Soma: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 9.17 is a hymn of 8 verses addressed to Soma. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 9, the hymns to Soma Pavamāna. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 674v-675r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 9.17.1-8 (aṣṭaka 6, adhyāya 8, varga 7); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 675r
translation.original_text:
1pra ni̱mnene̍va̱ sindha̍vo̱ ghnanto̍ vṛ̱trāṇi̱ bhūrṇa̍yaḥ | somā̍ asṛgram ā̱śava̍ḥ ||
2a̱bhi su̍vā̱nāsa̱ inda̍vo vṛ̱ṣṭaya̍ḥ pṛthi̱vīm i̍va | indra̱ṁ somā̍so akṣaran ||
3atyū̍rmir matsa̱ro mada̱ḥ soma̍ḥ pa̱vitre̍ arṣati | vi̱ghnan rakṣā̍ṁsi deva̱yuḥ ||
4ā ka̱laśe̍ṣu dhāvati pa̱vitre̱ pari̍ ṣicyate | u̱kthair ya̱jñeṣu̍ vardhate ||
5ati̱ trī so̍ma roca̱nā roha̱n na bhrā̍jase̱ diva̍m | i̱ṣṇan sūrya̱ṁ na co̍dayaḥ ||
6a̱bhi viprā̍ anūṣata mū̱rdhan ya̱jñasya̍ kā̱rava̍ḥ | dadhā̍nā̱ś cakṣa̍si pri̱yam ||
7tam u̍ tvā vā̱jina̱ṁ naro̍ dhī̱bhir viprā̍ ava̱syava̍ḥ | mṛ̱janti̍ de̱vatā̍taye ||
8madho̱r dhārā̱m anu̍ kṣara tī̱vraḥ sa̱dhastha̱m āsa̍daḥ | cāru̍r ṛ̱tāya̍ pī̱taye̍ ||
translation.text:
1LIKE rivers down a steep descent, slaying the Vr̥itras, full of zeal, The rapid Soma-streams have flowed.
2The drops of Soma juice effused fall like the rain upon the earth: To Indra flow the Soma-streams.
3With swelling wave the gladdening drink, the Soma, flows into.the sieve, Loving the Gods and slaying fiends.
4It hastens to the pitchers, poured upon the sieve it waxes strong At sacrifices through the lauds.
5Soma, thou shinest mounting heaven as 'twere above light's triple realm, And moving secm'st to speed the Sun.
6To him, the head of sacrifice, singers and bards have sung their songs, Offering what he loves to see.
7The men, the sages with their hymns, eager for help, deck thee strong steed, Deck thee for service of the Gods.
8Flow onward to the stream of meath rest efficacious in thy home, Fair, to be drunk at sacrifice.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 675r (numbered 97r by the scribe) (OPenn image 675, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 9.17.1 ‹āśavaḥ›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 675v (numbered 97v by the scribe), begins in RV 9.18.5 ‹ime iti rodasī iti›. Verses 9.17.1-8 end on this page; 9.17.1 begins on fol. 674v (numbered 96v by the scribe).
